title: The window, a month on
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Thursday. The twelve empty frames have been in the window five weeks. People have brought their own: a kid's face, a gull, the mail truck, the owner. Wood draws the window from inside for the whole hour before opening. Twelve pieces of a town.

panels.composition: The window from inside, early: twelve empty frames on the display shelf, and through each a piece of 101: gravel, a mailbox, the road, a spruce, sky.

image.prompt: the inside of a shop window with twelve empty picture frames of various sizes arranged on a shelf, each framing a different piece of the road, gravel and sky outside, black and white, no words

panels.composition: One frame: a KID's face pressed to the glass from outside, filling it.

image.prompt: close on an empty picture frame in a shop window with a child's face pressed to the glass filling it from outside, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Another: a gull on the gravel, exactly centered, as if it knew.

image.prompt: close on an empty picture frame in a window neatly containing a gull standing on gravel outside, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD's pad: the twelve frames, each with what was in it at ten AM. The OWNER behind him, looking. Twelve drawings. She takes the pad. She doesn't give it back till four.

image.prompt: a young man's drawing pad showing twelve small framed views, a woman in reading glasses taking the pad from his hands, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Twelve pieces of a town. She keeps the pad till four. (The window stays a year: dw_2000-04-25.)
